subject: Learning Methods
title: The Curse of Knowledge
description: A fast breakdown of The Curse of Knowledge for builders.

hook.text: A Stanford experiment asked tappers to knock a song's rhythm. They predicted 50 % of listeners would guess it.

buildup.text: The curse of knowledge: once you know something, you cannot imagine not knowing it. Experts lose the beginner's view.

discovery.text: This curse makes expert communication fail. Jargon, assumed context, and skipped steps confuse newcomers every time.

twist.text: The cure is teaching beginners. Their confusion forces you to remember what is actually hard about the material.

climax.text: When simplifying, assume zero background. Every term and step that seems 'obvious' was once unknown to you too.

punchline.text: Experts forget how it feels to not know. Teach to remember.

quiz.question: What is the 'curse of knowledge'?
options: Knowing too much makes you easily bored
Once you know something, you can't imagine not knowing it
Experts lose the ability to learn new things
